AppImage library extraction and source rebuild recipe

These instructions were written for Singhouse. inventory.json binds six x64
library files to exact Ubuntu binary packages and eighteen source-package
inputs. Its builder.extractionScripts entries record external provenance URLs
and hashes only. Those upstream scripts are not distributed here and are not
required by this recipe. This recipe does not cover the AppImage runtime itself.

Recover the distributed library bytes

1. For each libraries entry, obtain the binaryPackageUrl file and check its
   SHA256 against binaryPackageSha256 before extracting it. Work in a separate,
   empty directory for each package. dpkg-deb --extract PACKAGE DIRECTORY
   extracts package data without running maintainer scripts.
2. Inside each extracted package, select the regular file in the left column
   below. Copy its bytes into a separate application staging tree at the path
   in the right column. Each left path is relative to usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/.
   These are library files, not the package's SONAME symlinks.

   Package file                   Application path
   libgconf-2.so.4.1.5             usr/lib/libgconf-2.so.4
   libnotify.so.4.0.0              usr/lib/libnotify.so.4
   libappindicator.so.1.0.0        usr/lib/libappindicator.so.1
   libindicator.so.7.0.0           usr/lib/libindicator.so.7
   libXtst.so.6.1.0                usr/lib/libXtst.so.6
   libXss.so.1.0.0                 usr/lib/libXss.so.1

3. Check each staged file against the corresponding libraries[].sha256. The
   recorded buildId provides additional identification. Do not strip, relink,
   or otherwise transform these files when checking the distributed bytes.
   Retain the copyright and license directories supplied beside this recipe.

Build the library source packages

1. Check this source artifact's SHA256SUMS. Keep all sources/ files together;
   each of the six .dsc files names its upstream archive and Debian changes.
   inventory.json records their public URLs and SHA256 values. The .dsc
   signatures have not been verified; digest consistency is a separate check.
2. In an isolated working directory, use dpkg-source -x PATH/TO/PACKAGE.dsc
   for each package. It applies the included Debian changes to the upstream
   source. The resulting debian/ directory contains the package build rules
   and dependency declarations, including debian/rules and debian/control.
3. Prepare an amd64 Debian/Ubuntu build environment appropriate to the exact
   package version. Read its build dependencies, install them in that isolated
   environment, and use dpkg-checkbuilddeps in the extracted source tree to
   identify missing requirements. Then run dpkg-buildpackage -b -us -uc there
   to invoke the included package build rules and produce binary packages.
4. Inspect the resulting packages and extract the libraries using the mapping
   above. Rebuilt or modified binaries can have different hashes and build IDs;
   they cannot satisfy the existing release's exact binary inventory. A new
   release must record and review its new inputs and resulting identities.

The retained sources include upstream code and Debian packaging changes. This
recipe does not pin a historical build environment or claim a reproducible
rebuild; no rebuild has been established by creating the source artifact.
The artifact and these instructions do not establish public source delivery or
resolve whether additional corresponding-source materials are required.
